fields.title: قصر ابراہیم
fields.summary: مٹی کی دیواروں اور کھجور کے تنوں کی چھتوں والا قلعہ، جس کے اندر مسجد، سپاہیوں کی رہائش گاہیں اور برج یکجا ہیں۔
fields.body: ہفوف کے قلب میں قصر ابراہیم (یعنی ابراہیم کا محل) صدیوں کی تبدیلیوں کا گواہ بنا کھڑا ہے۔ یہ عیش و عشرت کا محل نہیں بلکہ ایک قلعہ ہے، جس کی ایک ہی فصیل کے اندر وہ کچھ اکٹھا ہے جو کم ہی یکجا ہوتا ہے: نفیس گنبد والی مسجد، سپاہیوں کی رہائش گاہیں، نگرانی کے برج، اصطبل اور گودام۔ اسے خلیجی خطے کے روایتی انداز میں تعمیر کیا گیا: دیواریں بھوسا ملی مٹی کی ہیں۔ چھتیں کھجور کے تنوں، شندل نامی لکڑی (جو کبھی خلیجی خطے میں درآمد کی جاتی تھی) اور پتھر کی ہیں۔ مینار کے اوپر تک پتھر کی چکر دار سیڑھیاں جاتی ہیں۔ اگر آپ اس کے کشادہ صحن میں گھومیں اور دیکھیں کہ گنبد محراب پر کیسے سایہ کیے ہوئے ہے، تو تاریخ کی وہ تہیں پڑھ لیں گے جو نسل در نسل جمتی چلی گئیں۔ آج یہ قلعہ الاحساء کے ورثے کے نمایاں ترین مقامات میں سے ایک ہے، اور شہر کی ان عمارتوں میں شامل ہے جن کی بنا پر 2018 میں الاحساء کے نخلستان کو یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست میں جگہ ملی۔

fields.summary: سعودی عرب کے مشرقی ساحل کی پہلی سمندری بندرگاہ، جہاں صحرا کی ریت خلیج کی نیلاہٹ سے جا ملتی ہے۔
fields.body: پکی سڑکیں بننے سے پہلے الاحساء کے لیے باہر کی دنیا کا دروازہ العقیر تھا۔ خلیج کے کنارے کی اس قدیم بندرگاہ پر کھجوروں اور سامان سے لدی کشتیاں لنگر ڈالتی تھیں، اور اسی کے راستے خبریں اور تجارت جزیرہ نما عرب کے قلب تک پہنچتی تھیں۔ آج العقیر میں دو ایسے منظر ملتے ہیں جو کم ہی یکجا ہوتے ہیں: صحرا سے پھیلتی چلی آتی نرم سفید ریت، اور خلیج کی شفاف نیلاہٹ جو وہیں سے شروع ہوتی ہے جہاں ریت ختم ہوتی ہے۔ مٹی کی عمارتوں کے آثار اور پرانا قلعہ آج بھی اس جگہ کی نگہبانی کر رہے ہیں، اور آنے والے کو یاد دلاتے ہیں کہ یہ پرسکون ساحل کسی زمانے میں ایسی چہل پہل کا مرکز تھا جو تھمنے کا نام نہ لیتی تھی۔ یہاں تاریخ بھی ہے اور ٹھہر کر سوچنے کا موقع بھی: آپ وہاں چل سکتے ہیں جہاں کبھی قافلے گزرتے تھے، اور اس ریت پر بیٹھ سکتے ہیں جو سمندر کو چھوتی ہے۔

fields.title: قصر صاہود
fields.summary: المبرز کے قلب میں سات برجوں والا ایک بہت بڑا دفاعی قلعہ، جو یونیسکو کی فہرست میں شامل الاحساء کے نخلستان کا ایک حصہ ہے۔
fields.body: المبرز کے قلب میں قصر صاہود کھڑا ہے: تقریباً 10,000 مربع میٹر پر پھیلا ایک بہت بڑا قلعہ۔ نگرانی کے سات برج اس کی چھ میٹر اونچی فصیلوں کی حفاظت کرتے ہیں، اور کبھی اس کے گرد ایک دفاعی خندق ہوا کرتی تھی۔ یہ بارہویں صدی ہجری کے اواخر میں تعمیر ہوا۔ اس قلعے نے اس مزاحمت کے واقعات دیکھے جو الاحساء نے علی پاشا کی لشکر کشی کے خلاف کی۔ اس کی فصیلوں کے اندر ایک مسجد، ایک کنواں، گودام، سپاہیوں کے کمرے اور اصطبل تھے، اور محاصرے کے دنوں میں شہر کے لوگ یہیں پناہ لیتے تھے۔ ورثہ کمیشن نے اس کی مرمت کی، اور آج یہ الاحساء کے نخلستان کے بارہ حصوں میں سے ایک ہے۔ یہ نخلستان 2018 میں یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست میں درج ہوا۔

accuracy.why: 'Al-Ahsa's first formal government school', flat, in an apposition as the source has it, the noun not widened; 1937 in the summary, both calendars in the body; the four places of the location all there. Two points off: «شروع ہوا» is the Arabic's verb where the English says 'opened' (ruling P23); the name carries a gloss the source does not write («(یعنی امیریہ اسکول)», the English title said in Urdu); 'stands on the rise' is 'the rise it is built on is called'.

nativeness.why: The second reader calls the page 'the clearest of the five in plain facts'; «اسکول» passed him in all three places, and the location sentences of round 1 too. Four points off: «تعلیمی بیداری» says little to either reader, «نامی بازار» beside «نامی مقام» is stiff to the second, and three edits are unread, the first sentence of the body recast in the judge's words.

compliance.why: «“بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام» as rulings P3b and P15 build it; the year pairs; the hours cell with «اتوار تا جمعرات» and « · »; the loan spelled as its entry. Two points off: four names of nine leaves are pending («مدرسہ امیریہ», «ام الخبیصی», «النعاثل», «بیت الثقافہ»), and the page has a second bracket form since this round, unproofed.

fit.why: The card was enough for both readers to plan with, and the common noun is the word they use. One point off: the title still says 'seminary' to this reader until the next line, and the gloss that answers it stands two lines further down, unread.

structure.why: Nine leaves in pack order; the labels «اوقات» and «فیس» are the approved pairs; 'Free entry' is «داخلہ مفت» as on qasr-ibrahim.

fields.title: مدرسہ امیریہ
fields.summary: الاحساء کا پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول، جو 1937 میں شروع ہوا۔ اس کی تاریخی عمارت آج ثقافت کا گھر ہے۔
fields.body: مدرسہ امیریہ (یعنی امیریہ اسکول)، الاحساء کا پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول، پرانے ہفوف کے مشرق میں، محلہ النعاثل میں واقع ہے۔ جس ٹیلے پر یہ بنا ہے اسے ام الخبیصی کہتے ہیں، اور سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار یہاں سے قریب ہے۔ اسکول میں پڑھائی 1356 ہجری (1937 عیسوی) میں کرائے کی ایک عمارت میں شروع ہوئی، اور اس کی مستقل عمارت 1360 ہجری (1941 عیسوی) میں کھلی۔ یہ عمارت عرب اسلامی طرز تعمیر میں بنی ہے: دروازہ محراب دار ہے اور اندرونی صحن کے گرد برآمدے ہیں۔ اس علاقے کے بچے نسل در نسل یہیں پڑھتے رہے۔ مرمت کے بعد یہ عمارت اب “بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام ہے، جو الاحساء کی تعلیمی بیداری کی یاد کو محفوظ رکھتا ہے۔
fields.area: محلہ النعاثل، پرانے ہفوف کے مشرق میں

blind_reader_rulings.reason: As the first reader's observation 2: the notice is the template's (b0-ui), and it names no channel (SD14 of the calibration). An artifact in part: on the built page the words are a link wherever the page has an operator link. Two readers of this batch and b2's have now said the same.

«اشتراک کریں» is an interface string of b0-ui, final after three readings there (its item N3: the loan is refused, the native verb is what the function is called on the phone and the browser); he 'understood at once'. His list of what read naturally is recorded for the interface: «یہ مقام محفوظ کریں» (which the first reader and b2's read first as 'protect'), the distance note, and the location message in its round-3 wording with 'check'.

Interface strings of b0-ui (det.nearby.h, det.nearby.d): approved pairs, not leaves of this batch. Carried to it: «سیر مکمل کر سکتے ہیں» has now been heard as translated by all four readers of the two attraction batches, and the two second readers each wrote a remedy («جہاں آپ اسی سیر میں جا سکتے ہیں», this one; «جنہیں آپ اپنی سیر میں شامل کر سکتے ہیں», b2's); both also call the heading above it advertisement voice.

As the first reader's observation 3: trails.partOf is b0-ui's, and 'Trails' reads as roads in the English too (logged there). He adds that «راستہ» also labels the breadcrumb: carried to the interface.

The same artifact of the plain-text page as the first reader's observation 5: the block is the home-page card, whose kicker is never rendered on the detail page; the tool still prints it after the back button. For the coordinator: two readers in a row have taken it for a second label of the page.

The template prints the component number bare after the badge, in every language; on a page with no date he took 1563 for a year, as the first reader did. Logged by b0-ui; nothing in the page fields can label it.

What a family needs on the spot (washrooms, parking, shade, a place to pray, food, the ground underfoot, whether one may swim) is in no source of the five pages. He says himself that he is reporting a lack, not asking the page to say more than it knows. Logged; nothing is supplied.

Ruling P17, not reopened: no vowel marks and no pronunciation gloss are written on a name (and the build guard rejects the kasra). The first reader and b2's said the same; the three remarks are on record for whoever may reopen it.

'Rarely' opens the praise of three pages because their sources do, and on qasr-ibrahim it is the site's own claim ('what rarely meets'), which the sister page undercuts. Round 1's «وہ کچھ اکٹھا ہے» is quoted here without a fault on its make: the wording passed him; what he doubts is the claim.

Applied in all six places of the batch (three sentences of qasr-ibrahim, the visiting row and one answer of the mosque page, the ameeriah summary): a full stop for each. Round 1 rejected the first reader's same remark (his observation 52) because he wrote the mark himself; a second reader who knew nothing of the first has now paused at it three times, and b2's second reader, on his own pages, says the same of the same mark. Ruled as item N33.

The cards differ in shape because the five sources carry different rows, and «علاقہ» is the template's label (b0-ui, ruling P27) over values that are a region, a village, a quarter and a coast in the sources themselves. His «کہاں ہے» is carried to the interface; «مقام» is taken there (it is the attraction in every interface string).

Two source wordings, two Urdu words: the bodies say 'in the heart of' («في قلب»), the area lines say 'Central' («وسط»). He calls both fine Urdu and only noticed the switch. One source word, one Urdu word is kept.

Who Ibrahim was, a century, a date or a builder are in neither source (the first reader's observation 7). His remark that the bracket says what 'an Urdu reader already hears in «قصر»' is recorded under P3c: the bracket stays because the source glosses the name and answers the gloss in the next sentence.

Applied: the summary no longer makes the fort the agent that 'brings together' its parts. His frame, with the verb of the answer that both readers passed («یکجا ہیں»). Round 1 had kept the line for the plural of owner ruling C39; the plural still shows, in «رہائش گاہیں» and the verb.

Applied for what is the Urdu's: the bare word that two readers took for a misspelling now carries its generic («شندل نامی لکڑی»), and 'imported to the Gulf' is said of the region. Which wood and from where are the owner-ruled explanation's silences (build check C40) and are logged again, now on two readers.

His remedy for the grammar: the condition is said at the start («اگر آپ …»). The picture (a dome shading the mihrab seen from the courtyard, layers of history with no history given) is the source's sentence and is logged, as for the first reader.

Applied in the body and in the answer. Round 1 kept «شہری تانے بانے» under ruling P25; that was too wide a reading of it: P25 protects how a claim is put (asserted or reported), and the claim stays asserted with the same cause. Two readers could not parse the image; it is said in his frame, with 'urban' kept as «شہر کی … عمارتوں».

'Daytime' against Friday's 4 to 8 pm, 'the light of the inner courtyard', and 'broad' against 'inner' for the courtyard are all the sources' (the first reader's observation 12). He could plan from the hours row, which is the Urdu's part.
The answer's second half is in both sources' answer (the first reader's observation 14).

'First seaport' is the owner's ruled wording (build check C34) with no sense of 'first' and no date; «سمندری بندرگاہ» is the source's 'seaport'. New from this reader: the line has no word for 'old' or 'former', so he took the port for a working one. Logged.

A label that says hours over a value with none; 'open public site'; whether the fort and the mud buildings are entered; 'remains' that may or may not stand: all as open in both sources (the first reader's observation 17).

'East of' without a distance, in the card and the answer, on three pages: the sources give no more (the first reader's observation 18). Whether «کے مشرق میں» is inside or outside is as open in the Arabic.
Applied: «جزیرہ نما عرب». Two readers found the bare word unfinished; the name is the reference title and has its entry now. Round 1 had waited for that entry.

Applied for the path, which the proof pass had named as a shift of meaning: no particular road is said now («وہاں … جہاں کبھی قافلے گزرتے تھے»). «ٹھہر کر سوچنے کا موقع» stays: it is the first reader's own wording for 'contemplation', the wording before it failed him, and this reader offers none. He calls the paragraph the most natural of the five, as the first did.

CONFIRMED again from the pack, by a second reader with the same grade: the only hours on the page are a park's, which the body never mentions; the mosque has none. Even under round 1's plain label he took the park's hours for the mosque's at first. Nothing is supplied.

Per person or not, why a range, and whether a family that wants only the mosque pays: none of it is in the sources. The form «10 سے 15 سعودی ریال» drew no remark: item N13 is confirmed by a second reader.

'What remains', 'was restored' and 'open to visitors' stand side by side in the sources, and whether one can pray there is the owner's unanswered question; no visiting time and no status is written (the first reader's observation 26).

The serious defect of round 1, seen by a second reader: the summary flat and 'after Medina', the body and the answer hedged and 'after the Prophet's Mosque', in both languages. Each field keeps its source's strength.

Applied in the body and in faq[2].a, not with his wording: inside the guarded clause the tribe would let 'the first place' be read as the tribe's first. The guarded clause ends at its own stop; the tribe has a sentence with a hedge of its own and a plain verb, so nothing restarts and nothing depends on a comma. «قبیلہ» is written before the name: two readers missed it. The frame is near the first reader's own remedy of round 1 («ادا کرنے والے بنو عبد القیس تھے جو اس سرزمین پر آباد تھے», his observation 27), with the hedge that remedy lacked.
No year, century or period for 'among the oldest', three times: in no source of the page (the first reader's observation 28).

Applied in the body and in faq[4].a: the quoted name is withdrawn. The prince's name comes first, as he asks; the name inflects; what the project is for has its own clause with the source's 'for'. His own form is not taken as written (it needs an izafat sign, which ruling P8 bars, and before «کے تحت» it would end on 'development under'). The pairing he found odd, as the first reader had («مساجد کی ترقی»), is not written: the name's word 'Development' is said with the everyday adjective, «تاریخی مساجد کے لیے ایک ترقیاتی منصوبہ».
The three sister mosques and their repetition in the answer are the sources' (the first reader's observation 31).

The closing sentence is the source's, image for image, in both languages; two readers have now heard it as an advertisement after a passage about the first Friday prayers. The register cannot be traded for the content (rulings P24, P25); the option goes to the owner with both readers named.

Applied for «اجتماع», which two readers in a row did not take in its plain sense: «مل بیٹھنے». Not applied for «حجم»: its dictionary entry gives 'size, bulk' first («جسامت، جُثّہ») and the physics sense after, and the figure it stands in is the source's.

The label is the source's 'Visiting', which tells no more than «زیارت» does, and a fee question on a mosque page is the source's FAQ. He sees why the word differs from «سیر» ('one does not «سیر» a mosque'): item N17 is confirmed.

Applied for the noun: «تقدس» (his word and the first reader's) for round 1's «حرمت». «ساتر لباس» stays, and the count is even: two readers wrote it in their own remedies (this batch's first and b2's first), two call it a word of the books of religious rulings (this one, minor, and b2's second on the twin row, moderate). The word says exactly 'modest'; the one word their two remedies share, «مناسب», says less, and they part on the rest. The options are on record in the VISITING-ROW entry. That the row is written for someone who has never entered a mosque is the owner-fixed row itself.

Ruling P9 as made in round 1: the city carries its epithet and nothing else follows; no sign of honour is written after «مسجد نبوی», whose entry is the reference title. He calls it taste and notes that newspapers write it bare.

CONFIRMED again from the pack, by a second reader with the same grade: the page says where the fort is and nothing else, and its interior is in the past tense. No status is asserted and no line is added. 'I would not take the family on this.'

His order: the place first, then the fort, as on qasr-ibrahim, with the verb he wrote himself («کھڑا ہے», the source's 'stands'). The seam was round 1's (the bracket between the two names went), and b2's second reader fell into the same one on two pages. What Al-Mubarraz is, is in neither source. The title itself drew no remark on palace and fort from this reader.

Applied in the summary and the body, in his words (the summary is stage 1's text again): the name is not frozen in quotation marks. Item N16 is amended. b2's second reader says the same of the same marks on khuzam. The frame of round 1 stays and passed him: he did not attach 2018 to the fort.
A Hijri century with no equivalent, in both sources; none is computed. A second reader has now taken it, on a quick read, for the twelfth century of the common era. Raised in the list for the owner.
Applied for the chain of possessives, which was round 1's (the first reader's order): the subject still leads and the chain is opened by a clause. Who Ali Pasha was is in neither source.

This is the test round 1 set for item N18: he could not tell whether «ادارہ ورثہ» names a particular body. The loan is admitted and the wording of stage 5 returns, «ورثہ کمیشن». Whose body it is stays unsaid, as in the source; a name of this kind takes no quotation marks.

As the first reader's observation 42: «بہت بڑا» twice is the source's 'massive' twice, in two fields each read alone; 'defensive citadel' is the source's pair; 'soldiers' quarters' here and 'barracks' on the other page are two source words. He finds the paragraph plain and easy to follow.

Settles a point of open item P3c that round 1 left out: by its own point (1) a gloss is owed on a page's own name whose generic says something else in Urdu. It stands at the first mention in the body, «مدرسہ امیریہ (یعنی امیریہ اسکول)»; the title stays bare. What «امیریہ» refers to is in neither source.

What the House of Culture is and what one sees there is in neither source, and the summary's 'a house of culture' is the source's phrase (the first reader's observation 45). He could plan the visit from the card.

«سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار» is the form ruled for a name met in passing whose generic is not an Urdu word; he understood it and found it stiff beside «نامی مقام», which is the frame of rulings P3b and P15. The two other forms each cost a reader more: the bracket lost the first reader the thread, and the bare name cost a reader of the interface the word that says it is a bazaar. The mound's name is the source's detail.
Applied: «بچے», the word both readers wrote. Round 1's ground for refusing it was wrong: the unmarked plural is as open as the Arabic's «أبناء».

Both points, in the one sentence that changes: the bracket and a comma part the name from «الاحساء», and the school is named in an apposition without a tense, as in the source, so that «ہے» no longer says it is a school today. That the summary does not say the school stopped is the source's.

proof_rulings.reason: Accepted, and answered at the root: item N16 is amended and the marks are withdrawn (the second reader read both marked places twice), so the guard no longer asks for what point (4) and the interface's bare structured-data name forbid. The new guard bans the marked form and is machine-read; the rest is written for the proofreader.

No string changes. The P10 entry is reworded as the proof suggests: b0-ui's clauses word for word under that batch's own letter ('its candidate B'), and the sentence on a figure below one lakh under this entry's letter A.

No string changes. All five corrections are made in termbase_final: (a) the ten shared entries are rebuilt on b0-ui's round-3 entries, with its closing sentences on «قصر ابراہیم» and «سوق القیصریہ»; (b) and (d) the notes of «بنو عبد القیس» and «قلعہ» are rewritten on the text as it stands; (c) b0-ui's own clause about b1 exercising the gender of «خلیج» is taken out, since b1 does not; (e) the four leaves of «تفریح گاہ» are named.
No string changes. The parsed clause of N7's guard stays word for word, and the scope is added after it: a range of days; two days joined by «اور» are not a range.

The text is kept: both blind readers read «جمعہ کو … ہفتے کو» without a remark, and the proof asks for no change. N7 now says which is which: «جمعہ» is written unchanged before a postposition, as in «جمعہ کی نماز»; «ہفتہ» takes its oblique.
No string changes. N13's guard now says that 'four-digit' is the checker's approximation of 'a year' and that a lifespan with a three-digit year is the proofreader's to pass.

(b) is the gap the second reader fell into: the school's name is glossed in its body, and point (3) now says why «قصر X» is exempt and «مدرسہ X» is not. (a) The ruling names what it amends (role file 05, items 2 and 10; gloss_regel; naming_policy.generic_nouns). (c) 'In the summary and the opening of the body', as b2's judge also found on khuzam.

(a) N18 is no longer ruled with its own reversal inside: the test was run, the loan is admitted, the entry cites P16. (b) N17 records that b2 ruled the word for visitors off a mosque page (its item N29). (c) N8 names the second untested proposal of P13 (5) and says it is not taken up. (d) N10 says whose the table is (the calibration's) and whose the 12-hour form (the owner's).

Borne out by the blind read to the letter: the possessive was read as 'the prince of'. The quoted name is withdrawn; the source's 'for' is back in a clause of its own, and the change is logged this time.

All three restored, each in the smallest way: (a) the door is Al-Ahsa's way to the outside world again (the same words in another order); (b) no particular road is said (change 9); (c) 'who settled this land' has its past tense again (change 10). They are counted off the accuracy line of round 1 and named in the change log.

No string changes. The notes are written afresh for this round and say what the checker reports now; P9 says in one line why the provisional key «مدینہ» is not listed as retired; the sahood compliance line no longer leans on a checker finding.

source_defects.where: jawatha-mosque summary against body and faq[2].a (first reader 24, serious; second reader 28)
source_defects.defect: One claim at two strengths and in two wordings, in both languages: the summary states flatly that the mosque is 'the first place a Friday prayer was held after Medina'; the body and the answer say it 'is said to be' the first 'after the Prophet's Mosque'. The summary is the page's search description and its index card, and its wording is not the one the owner ruled (build check C30: 'after the Prophet's Mosque').
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each field keeps its source's strength: flat in the summary, hedged in the body and the answer. Both readers saw it; the first said it made him doubt the rest, the second asks whether the claim is 'established or only a saying'.

source_defects.where: jawatha-mosque practical[0], practical[1], faq[0], faq[1] against the body (first reader 25, 26, 33; second reader 25, 26, 27, 35: serious for both)
source_defects.defect: The only hours and the only prices on the page are those of an adjacent park that the body never mentions; nothing says what the park is, whether the mosque stands inside it, whether the range is per person, when the mosque itself may be visited or whether one can pray there (the owner's question on working mosques is unanswered). 'What remains', 'was restored' and 'open to visitors' stand side by side; the FAQ asks whether a mosque charges a fee.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Translated as it stands; no hours, status or explanation is supplied. Even under a plain label the second reader took the park's hours for the mosque's at first. A family cannot tell whether the mosque is open or what it will be charged.

source_defects.where: sahood: the whole card (first reader 37; second reader 38: serious for both)
source_defects.defect: Since the stale status row was removed the page says where the fort is and nothing else: no hours, no fee, no FAQ, no word on whether it can be entered; the interior is described in the past tense.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The Urdu asserts no opening status and adds no line. Neither reader would take a family there on the strength of the page.

source_defects.defect: Nothing a family needs on the spot is said anywhere: washrooms, parking, shade or seating, a place to pray, food or drink, whether the ground suits small children or elderly parents, whether one may swim at Al-Uqair.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: None on the wording; nothing is supplied.

source_defects.where: sahood body: the date (first reader 39; second reader 41)
source_defects.defect: A Hijri century with no Gregorian equivalent, on a site that gives both calendars on another page and bare Gregorian years on this one.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: «بارہویں صدی ہجری کے اواخر میں», nothing computed. Both readers, reading fast, took it for the twelfth century of the common era and so made the fort some five centuries older than it is.

source_defects.defect: The English summary says the school 'opened in 1937' and that 'its historic building' is a house of culture; the body says classes began in 1937 in rented premises and the building opened in 1941. The English summary also drops the Hijri year the Arabic gives.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The summary says «جو 1937 میں شروع ہوا», the Arabic's verb (ruling P23); the second reader read it without the confusion the first had. The literal «جو 1937 میں کھلا» is on record.

source_defects.where: al-uqair practical[0], area, faq[1], body, summary (first reader 16 to 19; second reader 20 to 22)
source_defects.defect: A row labelled 'Hours & entry' with no hours; 'open public site' that does not say whether the fort and the mud buildings are entered or whether one may come after dark; 'east of Al-Ahsa' with no distance, in the card and again as the answer to 'where is it?'; nothing on what a family does there. 'First seaport' with no sense of 'first', no date and no word saying the port is a thing of the past.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each kept as open as the source; neither reader could plan the trip, and the second took the port for a working one until the body.

calibration.question: The gloss for a name whose Arabic generic is opaque or a false friend in Urdu («عین», «سوق», «قصر», and since round 2 «مدرسہ»), in running text: its form, and where it is owed.
candidates: A — the named gloss «(یعنی … کا …)» at the first body mention of every such name, passing mentions included (the text of stages 1 to 5)
B — the same form, owed only on the page whose own name it is; a passing mention stands bare
C — on a passing mention the Urdu generic in apposition after «نامی», no bracket
